title: VQE Validation on the Mononuclear T1 (Blue-Copper) Site: A Stepping Stone to the Multi-Copper Laccase Cluster
abstract: Validating variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) pipelines on realistic chemical systems is a critical stepping stone toward tackling classically intractable molecules. In this work, we report emulator-based validation of the VQE workflow proposed for the copper active site, executed on the LRZ Eviden Qaptiva emulator. A problem-tailored ADAPT-VQE with a full singles-doubles-triples (S+D+T) pool removes over 99% of the correlation error, reaching a stable plateau at 4.03 mEh relative to exact diagonalisation (148 selected operators). This establishes a >40x improvement over the hardware-efficient ansatz (HEA). Finally, we frame these emulator results as a robust baseline for upcoming physical quantum hardware runs on Euro-Q-Exa.
summary: This paper validates a Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) pipeline on a model of a copper enzyme active site, demonstrating that a problem-tailored ansatz significantly outperforms simpler methods. By achieving high accuracy on a manageable 18-qubit system, the authors establish a robust methodology necessary for tackling the full, classically intractable multi-copper enzyme cluster on future quantum hardware.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of simulating strongly correlated electronic structure in complex, open-shell transition metal active sites, which are classically intractable.
main_result: The problem-tailored ADAPT-VQE successfully validated a quantum computational pipeline, achieving a $>40	imes$ improvement in accuracy over simpler ansätze by removing over 99% of the correlation error.
method: The Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) algorithm was employed, utilizing a problem-tailored ansatz (ADAPT-VQE) to minimize the energy expectation value of the mapped Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the mononuclear T1 (Blue-Copper) active site of a laccase enzyme, modeled using a CAS(15e, 9o) active space and mapped to 18 qubits via the Jordan-Wigner transformation.
key_observables: Ground state energy ($E_0 = -2518.995 	ext{ Eh}$), energy convergence plateaus, and the relative improvement ratio ($> 40	imes$) between ansatz types.
important_parameters: The system size is limited to 18 qubits for validation, while the ultimate target requires 50–70 qubits, exceeding classical FCI memory limits.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the dynamically constructed, physically-motivated ansatz (ADAPT-VQE) represents the correct algorithmic path, despite the residual few-mEh gap suggesting limitations in the single-reference excitation ansatz.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy convergence of different ansätze (HEA vs. ADAPT-VQE) and demonstrate the exponential classical memory wall encountered when scaling to the full multi-copper cluster.
paper_structure: The paper first validates the VQE pipeline on the T1 site using an emulator, comparing HEA and ADAPT-VQE performance. It establishes the methodology's robustness before framing it as a necessary stepping stone for tackling the full, classically intractable multi-copper enzyme cluster.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the limitations of current quantum algorithms for simulating chemically relevant, strongly correlated open-shell systems, providing a concrete, validated roadmap for quantum chemistry hardware.
